items.title: Arc rail Phase 1: contracts deployed + one real session (Arc Testnet)
items.summary: GameRegistry and Randomness deployed to Arc Testnet (chain 5042002, USDC gas at 25 Gwei). One real session ran end to end: a match opened with a TTL, a dice seed was committed then revealed, rolls were derived from the seed, and the match settled. Both deploys cost about 0.023 USDC.
items.decision: Measurements only. No go-live decision here.

rows: a dice roll (derived from the seed)

items.title: Arc rail Phase 2: PlayerCore + self-hosted gasless relayer (Arc Testnet)
items.summary: PlayerCore deployed (the single per-player account: lives, points, premium, per-game buckets). The self-hosted relayer submitted every write and paid the gas; the player signed nothing and paid nothing. A full game cost 0.011034 USDC, all paid by the app. No paid sponsorship platform is used.
items.decision: Gasless model proven. Player cost is zero by construction.

items.title: Arc rail Phase 3: O(1) batching + TTL expiry (Arc Testnet)
items.summary: One transaction commits a Merkle root for N games, so the gas is flat (O(1)) and the per-game cost falls as 1/N. TTL was proven live: a game opened with a 2 second TTL was expired permissionlessly after the deadline.
items.decision: Batching is the cost lever. The window policy is a config choice.

items.title: Arc rail settlement window: launch economics
items.summary: The relayer flushes when the pending batch reaches N games OR the window reaches T seconds, whichever first, and always flushes at window close even with one game. This table shows what a window costs at very low launch volume (10 games a day).
items.decision: Proposed launch setting: T=24h, N=100 (adjustable). No decision recorded yet.

sections.heading: Cost per window at 10 games a day
When volume grows (N flushes first)
bullets: Receipts while a batch is open: each game gets an instant app-signed receipt (including the dice-seed hash published before the game), labelled pending; at flush it upgrades to an on-chain receipt with that game's own Merkle proof and the batch transaction hash. No game waits on another.
To have an on-chain link the moment a game ends, a config knob anchors each start on-chain for about 0.00243 USDC (about 1 USD per 400 games at launch volume).
